17.t: Working with data: drop height and drag
q: Calculate the mean speed for 2 and for 8 cases.
Explain why stacking cases makes them fall faster.
More cases means more weight but the same shape and area, so drag must be larger to balance it: they reach a higher terminal speed.
Doubling the cases did not double the speed. Suggest why.
Drag rises faster than speed (roughly with the square of the speed), so a small speed rise balances the extra weight. (Also the cases may not reach terminal speed in 2 m.)
